title: Do Eden Anyway: Wife
thesis: The spouse we long to enjoy becomes enjoyable only when we express commitment, investment, and effort—primarily through speaking the gospel, God's promises, and words of love—so that marriage becomes a lifelong partnership of mutual sanctification and praise.

title: Do Eden Anyway: Work
thesis: Your work—across all domains of life—is your theology on display, and transformation in work comes not by sheer willpower but by renewed knowledge of and fellowship with the God who is for you.

title: The Earthy Piety of Providence
thesis: In a world marked by uncertainty and unfairness, we are called to do Eden anyway—faithfully discharging our God-given duties in work, celebration, relationships, and worship, trusting that our creaturely limitations and the brokenness around us do not change what we are or what we are for.

title: Yet I Know
thesis: Wisdom — rooted in knowing God rather than merely observing circumstances — insulates believers from the seductive lie that the prosperity of the wicked proves there is no God or that fearing God is futile.

title: Lessons from the House of Mourning
thesis: Death forces us to face reality, and those who lay it to heart become wise.

title: Choose Well, Trust Well
thesis: When you have a choice to make, wisdom helps you choose well; when you have no choice, wisdom helps you trust well—but wisdom without humility spoils into folly.
